jobs.title: Director, Enterprise Transformation Enablement
jobs.description: Who We Are We're powering a cleaner, brighter future. Exelon is leading the energy transformation, and we're calling all problem solvers, innovators, community builders and change makers. Work with us to deliver solutions that make our diverse cities and communities stronger, healthier and more resilient. We're powered by purpose-driven people like you who believe in being inclusive and creative, and value safety, innovation, integrity and community service. We are a Fortune 200 company, 20,000 colleagues strong serving more than 10.7 million customers at six energy companies -- Atlantic City Electric (ACE), Baltimore Gas and Electric (BGE), Commonwealth Edison (ComEd), Delmarva Power & Light (DPL), PECO Energy Company (PECO), and Potomac Electric Power Company (Pepco). We're committed to creating an environment where every person can thrive. Our employee experience is grounded in four tenets that guide how we support our people: purposeful careers, growth opportunities, community impact, and support to thrive. In our relentless pursuit of excellence, we elevate diverse voices, fresh perspectives and bold thinking. And since we know transforming the future of energy is hard work, we provide competitive compensation, incentives, excellent benefits and the opportunity to build a rewarding career. Are you in? Primary Purpose What if Exelon could redesign itself as fast as the energy industry is changing? The Director, Enterprise Transformation Enablement exists to make that possible. This newly created enterprise role is the architect of how Exelon organizes, adapts and works in an AI-enabled future. It combines change leadership, organizational design and work redesign into one integrated capability. Working with the Transformation Office to co-develop Exelon's multi-year transformation roadmap, this leader will redefine work across the enterprise. That means redefining workflows, rebalancing work between people and AI agents, and building structures that are leaner, faster and more effective. Along the way, they will build an enterprise-wide change capability that helps employees and leaders handle change with confidence. The goal goes beyond managing change. It is to make adaptability a competitive advantage for Exelon, delivering breakthrough results for customers, communities and employees. **This is a multiple‑location posting. The selected candidate may be based out of our Exelon Corporate Office locations in IL, DC, MD, or PA** Primary Duties Co-develop enterprise transformation agenda and lead supporting enterprise change strategy. Collaborate with the Transformation Office in Finance to jointly develop a multi-year transformation roadmap. Define and lead the supporting enterprise change management strategy, standards, and governance for the transformation portfolio. Build an integrated change roadmap spanning sponsorship activation, stakeholder engagement, communications, readiness, adoption, and sustainment. Establish the central methodologies, playbooks, and toolkits using practical approaches that will resonate with employees across all levels, leveraging structured approaches (e.g., Prosci/ADKAR, Kotter) when appropriate. Collaborate with HR, executives and people leaders to execute these strategies in the business, ensuring a consistent, disciplined, and measurable approach across operating companies. Partner with Employee Listening team to track employee engagement related to change management, with a goal of achieving measurable gains. Advance the shift from episodic to continuous, proactive, and agile change system embedded in the flow of work. Lead operating model and organizational design governance and oversight. Develop and own the enterprise approach, principles, and processes for operating model and organizational design transformation, including structure, spans and layers, decision rights, role leveling (in partnership with Total Rewards), and accountability models. Create scalable frameworks, diagnostics, and tools that HR and business leaders can apply to redesign organizations in the business, balancing “One Exelon” consistency with business differences. Advise senior leaders on org design choices that improve agility, effectiveness, outcomes, and cost. Lead work redesign for AI and the future of work. Lead the strategy, standards, and processes for redesigning work as AI, automation, and agentic capabilities are deployed across the enterprise. Establish methods for task and role decomposition, human + machine (agent) work rebalancing, and skills-based work models that maximize human–AI convergence and ROI. Partner with Strategic Workforce Planning, Enterprise Learning, Technology/AI, and the business to align the right talent to the right work and equip HRBPs to execute role and work redesign at scale. Build change and org design capability across the enterprise. Build change, org design, and work-redesign capability at scale by equipping and enabling HRBPs, people leaders, and transformation practitioners. Develop training, certification pathways, communities of practice, and reusable assets that raise enterprise fluency and reduce reliance on external consultants. Measure adoption, governance, and continuous improvement. Establish enterprise metrics for change adoption, benefit realization, and ROI, and monitor cumulative change load/saturation across the transformation portfolio to protect workforce well-being and delivery. Provide executive leadership with data-driven insights on the change portfolio and related tradeoffs, risks, benefits, and critical decisions. Continuously improve standards, tools, and processes based on outcomes and stakeholder feedback. Lead and develop a high-performing team. Provide leadership, direction, and development for the Transformation Enablement team as outlined in the organizational structure. Foster collaboration, accountability, and innovation, and serve as a visible enterprise leader representing Exelon’s culture and values. Job Scope Leads a Center of Excellence team of approximately 5 FTEs, including a Senior Manager, Transformation & Enterprise Change (E05); Manager, Change & Organizational Design (E04); Manager, Role & Work Redesign (E04); and a Cross-Capability (E03) resource. Reports to the Vice President, Talent (E09) and serves as a member of the Talent COE Leadership Team. Interfaces with all levels of the organization, including senior executives, HRBPs, and HR leaders across Exelon’s operating companies (ComEd, BGE, PECO, PHI/ACE/DPL/Pepco, and Corporate/BSC). Sets enterprise standards, strategy, and processes for change management, organizational design, and work redesign that HRBPs in the business execute, driving enterprise-wide impact through collaboration, influence, and consultative leadership. Collaborates with Enterprise and Operating Company functional teams to co-develop “One Exelon” solutions that provide flexibility for true business differences. Able to travel up to 25% Minimum Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources, Organizational Development, Business, or a related field. Minimum of 12 years of progressive experience in change management, organizational design/effectiveness, transformation, or organizational development in a large, matrixed organization. Minimum of 5 years of supervisory experience. Demonstrated success designing and leading enterprise-wide change management and organizational design strategies aligned to business outcomes. Expertise in structured change methodologies (e.g., Prosci/ADKAR, Kotter) and organizational design principles (operating model, structure, spans and layers, decision rights). Experience redesigning work, roles, and processes—including in the context of AI, automation, or digital transformation—to improve productivity and effectiveness. Proven ability to build enterprise standards, playbooks, and tools that are executed by HR Business Partners and business leaders. Strong ability to apply data and analytics to measure adoption, benefit realization, and ROI. Strong collaboration and influencing skills across multiple HR functions and operating companies; strategic, consultative, and creative mindset. Exceptional communication, storytelling, facilitation, and stakeholder management skills, with demonstrated ability to engage senior leaders. Demonstrated ability to lead, coach, and develop a high-performing team. Preferred Qualifications Master’s degree in Business, HR, Organizational Development, or Organizational Psychology. Change management certification (e.g., Prosci/ADKAR, CCMP) and/or organization design certification. Experience leading work redesign for AI/agentic augmentation and building skills-based work models. Experience building a Center of Excellence, transformation office, or enterprise change function. Experience in the energy or utility sector, including union environments and frontline/safety-critical workforces. Familiarity with enterprise transformation partnerships (e.g., major consulting firms) and future-of-work research and benchmarks. Benefits Annual salary will vary based on a candidate’s skills, qualifications, experience, and other factors: $174,400.00/Yr. – $239,800.00/Yr. plus an additional $50K in Long Term Incentive Plan annually Annual Bonus for eligible positions: 30% 401(k) match and annual company contribution Medical, dental and vision insurance Life and disability insurance Generous paid time off options, including vacation, sick time, floating and fixed holidays, maternity leave and bonding/primary caregiver leave or parental leave Employee Assistance Program and resources for mental and emotional support Wellbeing programs such as tuition reimbursement, adoption and surrogacy assistance and fitness reimbursement Referral bonus program And much more Note: Exelon-sponsored compensation and benefit programs may vary or not apply based on length of service, job grade, job classification or represented status. Eligibility will be determined by the written plan or program documents.

Primary Purpose PRIMARY PURPOSE OF POSITION Assist in the development, delivery, and management of energy efficiency programs as part of the state utility commission approved energy efficiency portfolio to ensure cost recovery and minimize performance risk. Responsible for the end-to-end management and successful execution of a behind-the-meter residential battery pilot program in Delaware. Duties include overseeing customer acquisition and marketing efforts, coordinating dispatch operations, managing program reporting and performance metrics, administering program budgets, and ensuring prudent financial management and regulatory compliance. Primary Duties PRIMARY DUTIES AND ACCOUNTABILITIES Work with Planners and Evaluation Team to participate in the development of energy efficiency programs including evaluation of energy efficiency measures, design of programs, outreach to stakeholders and the marketplace, and filing of requirements. Manage the process of procuring services from subcontractors and vendors specializing in delivering energy efficiency programs to utility customers. This includes issuing RFP's, evaluating responses, identifying best offers, obtaining legal review, coordinating with Supply Services, and awarding contracts. Provide ongoing oversight of providers. Develop performance metrics applicable to each individual energy efficiency program and in conformance with the overall portfolio. Conduct regular subcontractor and vendor meetings and obtain progress reports to ensure expectations. Track performance and provide feedback and corrective actions as necessary. Work with Marketing Promotions team in managing all program communication and outreach needs. Work to make certain that all messaging is accurate and consistent with the larger energy efficiency portfolio. Recruit market partners such as retailers, builders, energy raters and auditors, and other trade allies for market outreach. Maintain relationships with partners to maximize program performance. Conduct training as needed to expand the program delivery network. Prepare program status reports to accurately monitor progress toward program performance and financial goals. Maintain and provide appropriate documentation to support regulatory compliance filings. Ensure that mechanisms exist for controlling programs' progress toward goals: such mechanisms should manage the risk of either under-achieving or over-achieving goals, consistent with the portfolio plan. Ensure that Accounts Payable (invoice review, verification and check creation) and Accounts Receivable functions (audit billing) are managed according to applicable Corp. Policies and Procedures and comply with appropriate accounting and Sarbanes Oxley rules. Job Scope JOB SCOPE Assist in planning, and subsequently implement and manage energy efficiency programs as part of a portfolio approved by the state utility commission. Fulfill the day-to-day requirements to serve customers participating in energy efficiency programs. Hire and provide daily oversight of various sub-contractors and program fulfillment vendors. Develop the necessary performance metrics and track them to ensure that programs are delivered according to state utility commission rules and regulations to ensure cost recovery. Ensure that Company exposure to litigation risk is minimized. Manage all customer relations' issues arising out of energy efficiency programs. Provide data analysis and subject matter expertise in responding to state utility commission requests or implementation of state utility commission orders. This includes annual reporting of results. Number of personnel managed (direct): none, (indirect): numerous contractors and vendors delivering programs. Minimum Qualifications MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS Bachelor's degree in Business or Engineering and 4-7 years of energy conservation / energy efficiency work experience OR in lieu of degree, 6-9 years energy conservation / energy efficiency experience is required. Demonstrated ability to work within established budgets and deliver promised results. Thorough understanding of utility cost recovery mechanisms. Ability to communicate with and coordinate with a wide variety of professionals ranging from engineers to vendors, to subcontractors. Preferred Qualifications PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS Experience developing and delivering utility energy efficiency programs to specific sector. Program and contract management experience are preferred. Benefits Annual salary will vary based on a candidate’s skills, qualifications, experience, and other factors: $89,600.00/Yr. – $123,200.00/Yr. Annual Bonus for eligible positions: 15% 401(k) match and annual company contribution Medical, dental and vision insurance Life and disability insurance Generous paid time off options, including vacation, sick time, floating and fixed holidays, maternity leave and bonding/primary caregiver leave or parental leave Employee Assistance Program and resources for mental and emotional support Wellbeing programs such as tuition reimbursement, adoption and surrogacy assistance and fitness reimbursement Referral bonus program And much more Note: Exelon-sponsored compensation and benefit programs may vary or not apply based on length of service, job grade, job classification or represented status. Primary Purpose The Principal Business Program Manager is a critical member of BGE’s Project Initiation Team, responsible for establishing centralized ownership, visibility, and escalating early-stage and portfolio-wide project risk for major Transmission and Substation capital projects. Partnering closely with Project Initiation leadership, Project Controls, Engineering, Planning, Finance, and Investment Strategy, this role leads risk identification during project initiation, develops and maintains standardized risk registers, and provides portfolio-level risk insights to inform governance decisions, capital forecasting, mitigation planning, and leadership escalation. By integrating risk, scope, schedule, and cost perspectives, this role strengthens project readiness, improves financial predictability, and ensures critical risks are identified, quantified where possible, assigned to accountable owners, and escalated before they impact execution, regulatory outcomes, or portfolio performance. The ideal candidate will possess demonstrated Transmission and Substation project experience, strong front-end project development expertise, and the ability to lead cross-functional risk management practices across complex utility capital portfolios. In addition, this role is responsible for portfolio-level risk monitoring across all centrally managed Transmission projects supported by PIT. The Principal Business Program Manager maintains a consolidated view of risk exposure, identifies systemic issues and emerging threats, tracks time-sensitive risks and decision points, and monitors mitigation commitments to ensure risks do not go unmanaged as projects progress from initiation. through execution. Acting as an early-warning and portfolio governance function, not a project firefighter, the role ensures the right risks are elevated to the right stakeholders at the right time, enabling proactive leadership decisions, stronger Investment Strategy coordination, and improved portfolio accountability. The Principal Business Program Manager does not perform project execution activities. Instead, the role enables successful execution by ensuring that risks are clearly understood, assessed for probability and impact, quantified where practical, assigned to owners, linked to mitigation strategies, and aligned with governance expectations prior to project handoff. This position plays a key role in transforming fragmented, siloed initiation practices into a disciplined, transparent, and enterprise-aligned project initiation and risk management framework. Position may be required to work extended hours for coverage during storms or other energy delivery emergencies. Primary Duties Develop, manage, and continuously improve PIT’s portfolio-wide project risk management framework, including risk identification practices, standardized risk register requirements, probability and impact assessment criteria, escalation thresholds, reporting cadence, and governance expectations. (25%) Lead structured risk identification with cross-functional stakeholders across Planning, Engineering, Project Controls, Finance, Investment Strategy, Project Management, Legal, Real Estate, Regulatory, and other supporting organizations. Apply risk identification techniques including workshops, interviews, assumptions analysis, lessons learned reviews, dependency mapping, readiness reviews, and review of scope, schedule, cost, permitting, regulatory, outage, constructability, and stakeholder inputs. (20%) Coordinate risk mitigation strategies with Investment Strategy, Finance, Engineering, Planning, Project Controls, and project risk owners to align risk exposure with capital planning, authorization timing, contingency assumptions, prioritization decisions, and mitigation commitments. (15%) Track risk owners, mitigation commitments, aging risks, overdue actions, escalation items, decision deadlines, and risks requiring leadership intervention. Ensure the portfolio risk register remains current and actionable rather than a static reporting tool. (10%) Develop, organize, and present portfolio-level risk reporting, performance reports, dashboards, executive narratives, and decision-support materials leadership, governance forums, and Investment Strategy discussions. (10%) Drive risk management process improvement by developing templates, guidance, training materials, recurring review routines, and quality checks that strengthen risk ownership, accountability, and consistent use of risk information across the project initiation lifecycle. (5%) Provide expert analytical, operational, and program management support to the Project Initiation Team, with emphasis on portfolio risk management, governance discipline, cross-functional alignment, and executive-ready communication. (5%) Manage large and or highly complex and often unique projects requiring application of established project management principles and techniques. Directly accountable to deliver project on time and at or below budget. (10%) Job Scope This is an individual contributor position that works independently with little or no supervision. The position requires integration of business knowledge, utility Transmission and Substation experience, project initiation practices, project controls principles, investment planning considerations, and functional priorities to address complex, non-standard portfolio risks and business situations. The position regularly mentors less experienced colleagues and supports process maturity across cross-functional project teams. Position requires routine interaction with key internal and external stakeholders, executives, directors, managers, and staff across the organization. The role is responsible for portfolio risk ownership, risk visibility, mitigation coordination, and risk reporting, but does not replace the Execution responsibilities of project managers, engineers, estimators, schedulers, or functional risk owners. Position may require working extended hours and or shift work to support business operations. Minimum Qualifications Bachelor's Degree in a business or S.T.E.M. field with a minimum of 7-10 years relevant experience. Advanced knowledge and understanding of applicable standards, methods, processes and practices, business fundamentals, and performance metrics in the specific functional area supported by this position (e.g., electric or gas operations, customer service, transmission and substation, distribution system operations, regulatory and external affairs). Advanced proficiency in standard software applications (e.g., Microsoft Project, Visio, Excel, & PowerPoint), and relevant specialized business applications (e.g., project portfolio management, requirements/test management, CIS/CRM, customer self-service, telephony, EPS, EAM, work management, & outage management) to support business needs. Demonstrated business acumen and ability to create value with advanced problem solving, financial/analytical, performance management, negotiation, and conflict management skills. Demonstrated ability to lead a cross-functional team. Demonstrated ability to build consensus, establish trust, meet critical deadlines, communicate effectively, and foster culture change. Customer driven with demonstrated excellent written and oral communication skills and ability to interact with people of all levels. Demonstrated ability to develop and implement process enhancements and efficiencies including new technology In lieu of degree, 9-12 years of relevant experience. Preferred Qualifications PMP, PMI-RMP, CAPM, Six Sigma, or equivalent project, program, process improvement, or risk management certification. Master’s degree in business administration, Finance, Economics, Engineering, Public Policy, Risk Management, Program Management, or related discipline, with coursework or focus areas on risk management, capital planning, portfolio management, project controls, or enterprise decision-making. Demonstrated experience in portfolio-level risk management, including development and maintenance of standardized risk matrices or registers, aggregation of project-level risks into a consolidated portfolio view, and identification of systemic or cross-cutting risks impacting capital delivery. Experience supporting front-end project initiation or feasibility activities, with strong understanding of how early-stage scope, schedule, cost, outage, permitting, regulatory, constructability, and stakeholder decisions influence downstream execution and financial outcomes. Proven ability to partner with Investment Strategy, Finance, Capital Planning, or Portfolio Management organizations to translate risk exposure into financial risk and opportunity implications, cash flow considerations, contingency assumptions, prioritization input, and capital portfolio guidance. Experience developing risk reporting, dashboards, metrics, or analytics using tools such as Power BI, Excel-based models, or similar platforms to communicate portfolio risk trends, escalation points, mitigation status, and decision triggers. Demonstrated ability to operate as an independent portfolio risk steward by monitoring risk status, tracking mitigation commitments, coordinating with accountable owners, and proactively escalating time-sensitive risks without owning execution-level resolution. Experience working within a regulated utility environment, particularly Transmission or large capital project portfolios, with understanding of regulatory, permitting, external stakeholder, reliability, outage, and capital recovery risks. Strong stakeholder engagement and facilitation skills, including the ability to influence cross-functional teams across Planning, Engineering, Project Controls, Project Management, Investment Strategy, Finance, Legal, Real Estate, and external partners. This will involve setting up kick off and challenge meetings with the appropriate subject matter experts, (SMEs) their Key Managers and assimilating all information with appropriate signoffs. All documents shall be posted to an evidence/artifact storage location. (15%) Evaluate, determine, and report utility compliance to Exelon Utility procedures, standards and requirements. Recommend enhancements to current practices and procedures to drive continuous improvement as well as a Culture of Compliance within the business unit. (10%) Responsible for creating mitigation plans and monitoring progress through action tracking and timely updates on each. (10%) Ensure necessary work activities for the OTSGP as well as TSA (Transportation Security Administration) Cyber Security directive compliance are initiated in the Work Management system, executed using procedures and tracked in systems with documented completion evidence. (10%) Provide analysis and support to leadership for the OTSGP as well as TSA (Transportation Security Administration) Cyber Security directive compliance program including ongoing reporting of performance improvements, organizational initiatives and compliance related communications. (10%) Build and maintain knowledge of current Cyber Security controls and directives Impacting Gas OT systems and devices as defined in the OT Security Governance program as well as the TSA compliance directives. (10%) Lead/participate in compliance audits. Plan, prepare and execute audit tasks and support audit teams. Compiles and creates evidence packages in preparation for audit activities. (10%) Represent Exelon Utilities on select committees to facilitate benchmarking and continuous improvement. Participate in standards review processes. (10%) Job Scope The Sr. Gas Operations Compliance Specialist evaluates and determines compliance for Exelon Utilities activities, will recommend corrective actions and assist in the development procedures to address inadequacies that are discovered during assessments, including recommendations that are administrative or functional in nature. Will typically involve acting in a consulting or advisory capacity and gather commitments of other management personnel in the organization as well as collaborate with other OpCo's for consistency and alignment within cyber programs. The Sr. Gas Operations Compliance Specialist acts as liaison to the OTSGP Exelon team and the TSA for compliance issues, tracks OTSGP and TSA activities and consults/advises key Exelon personnel in order to develop strategic direction for compliance to OTSGP and TSA standards. The Sr. Gas Operations Compliance Specialist generally operates with wide latitude on action and decision-making. Minimum Qualifications Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science, Business Administration, Engineering or related field and 5-8 years experience working in any combination of gas operations, regulatory, legal or financial disciplines. OR in lieu of a bachelor's degree, a minimum of 9-12 years of relevant business experience. Ability to analyze, interpret, and determine compliance requirements associated with Operational Technology Security Governance program (OTSGP) as well as TSA (Transportation Security Administration) Cyber Security compliance directives and ability to apply problem solving approaches. Knowledge and use of computer systems and applications with Word/Access/Excel/PowerPoint/Passport. Along with excellent written, oral communication and analytical skills. Preferred Qualifications Degree in Computer Science, Business, Engineering or related field knowledge and experience with utility regulations, guides, standards, codes, methods, practices, engineering principles. Knowledge of process control systems and incorporation of Management of Change practices into cyber compliance programs.
